title: Gettysburg, Panama and preserving worn band music
summary: Clark explains that the Gettysburg parts faded and became greasy. The interviewers offer to copy his music for Tulane. They discuss Panama and its added high trumpet part.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well look at Gettysburg, what did you tell me about that? I think you were the one who was telling me how you wore it out.
Oh yeah, we played Gettysburg. That's a good march.
You never play it anymore though, huh?

Well I'll tell you what happened. You see those cards, they got so faded and they turned, they changed colors on us. You see. And then you know those fellas making those stops and they eat their hands, be greasy, you know, and they put their hands on the card and there it is. You see.

Well we could get copies made of those, why we'd like to do that, you know, and keep them on file at Tulane. So you, and seal them up, you know, and if you, if you want to have them refer to them again, you got it. We could do that, you know.
Well let me see. Not give them to anybody else. Now, uh, I think it's Barnhouse. I'm not sure. But there's one of those houses that publishes that. I don't know whether it's Barnhouse or Fillmore.
It publishes which? Gettysburg.
Gettysburg.
But I mean if ever there's a piece, you know, that you can't replace, we'll get copies of it made because you know we'd like to keep a copy. I said we've got a camera specially made. You know.
You see like Gettysburg, like Gettysburg, American Soldier, Panama, those marches are standard. Panama is a standard. They played that when I was a boy.
And it was written, huh?

Yeah it was written but I don't know what happened to it. The fellas got so used to it that they really don't use the music of it anymore. But it was written. By whom I don't know. Do you remember High Society? You ever seen the music for that when you were in high society?
No I never did see the music of High Society.
I wonder if all the parts that you play in Panama are on the music, if they made up new parts
or what? That's very hard to see. It'd be interesting to look into that.
We'll find the music sometime for the marches. Because it is, I think they added a part.
They added a part to Panama?
Yeah they hit a high note and then go down. You know that trumpet part?
I see.
Because a tubo player I know on the west coast told me, he says that's not on the rhythm.
